title: How requests sends one HTTP call
lead: What happens between `requests.get(url)` and the `Response` you get back, traced from the psf/requests source. The library is about 6,400 lines of Python; this page is the part you need to reason about timeouts, redirects, credentials and connection reuse.
status: As built: psf/requests main at commit 3c7baaa (26 Oct 2026). Timeout and redirect behaviour checked by probe against requests 2.34.2.

blocks.text: Every call goes through a `Session`, even `requests.get()`: it creates a throwaway session for that one call. The session merges your arguments with its own settings and the environment, hands the request to an adapter chosen by URL prefix, and the adapter hands it to urllib3.

blocks.title: From requests.get() to Response
blocks.alt: A top-to-bottom flow: build Request, prepare it, merge environment, pick adapter, send through urllib3, run hooks and save cookies, follow redirects, then download the body unless streaming.
blocks.caption: The main path runs down the middle. Red boxes on the left are where the call ends in an exception; the redirect loop on the right sends again through the same adapter.

nodes.title: requests.get(url, ...)
nodes.tip: A module-level helper. It opens a brand-new Session in a `with` block and closes it on return, so no connection is reused between two `requests.get()` calls.

nodes.title: Build a Request
nodes.tip: Session.request() packs your arguments into a plain `Request` object. Nothing is encoded or merged yet.

nodes.title: Prepare it
lines: merge session headers, params, cookies, auth
nodes.tip: prepare_request() merges per-call values over the session's. If no auth was given and trust_env is on, it looks in ~/.netrc. The result is a PreparedRequest with the URL, headers and body encoded.

nodes.title: Merge environment settings
lines: proxies, CA bundle, stream, verify, cert
nodes.tip: With trust_env on, HTTP(S)_PROXY / NO_PROXY and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or CURL_CA_BUNDLE are read here. A per-call value always wins over the session's, which wins over nothing.

nodes.title: Pick adapter by URL prefix
nodes.tip: The session holds adapters keyed by prefix, longest first. New sessions mount one HTTPAdapter for `https://` and one for `http://`; `mount()` lets you add a custom one, e.g. with retries.

nodes.title: InvalidSchema
nodes.tip: No mounted prefix matches, for example `ftp://` or a typo like `htps://`.

nodes.title: HTTPAdapter.send()
nodes.tip: Gets a connection from urllib3's pool (10 per host by default) and sends. Retries default to 0, and with no timeout argument it waits for the server forever.

nodes.title: ConnectionError, Timeout, SSLError ...
nodes.tip: urllib3's errors are translated into requests' own exception classes, so callers only need to catch `requests.exceptions.RequestException`.

nodes.title: Run response hooks, save cookies
nodes.tip: Your `hooks={'response': ...}` functions run here, before redirects are followed. Set-Cookie headers go into the session's cookie jar so the next request sends them.

nodes.title: Redirect, and allowed?
nodes.tip: A redirect is a 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308 with a Location header. allow_redirects defaults to True for every method except HEAD.

nodes.title: Rebuild request for new URL
nodes.tip: resolve_redirects() copies the request, changes method, body and headers for the new URL, then sends it again with allow_redirects=False. Each response joins `r.history`.

nodes.title: stream=True?
nodes.tip: Without stream, the whole body is read into memory before you get the Response. With stream, the connection stays checked out until you read the body or close the response.

nodes.title: Download the whole body
nodes.tip: Touching `r.content` reads the socket to the end and returns the connection to the pool.

nodes.title: Response
nodes.tip: Carries status, headers, body (or an open stream), `elapsed`, and `history` of any redirects. A 4xx or 5xx is still a normal Response: call `raise_for_status()` to turn it into an exception.

blocks.text: Redirects are where requests quietly changes your request. It follows browsers rather than the letter of the RFC, and it protects credentials when the host changes.

blocks.title: One pass of resolve_redirects()
blocks.alt: A loop: check redirect count, rewrite the method, drop the body for most codes, drop Authorization if the host changed, re-add cookies and proxies, send again.
blocks.caption: Each pass rewrites a copy of the previous request. The amber steps change what your server receives.

nodes.title: Response with Location
nodes.tip: get_redirect_target() reads the Location header only when the status is a redirect code.

nodes.title: 30 redirects already?
nodes.tip: Counted per call. The old response body is read and its connection released first, so long chains don't exhaust the pool.

nodes.title: TooManyRedirects
nodes.tip: The exception carries the last response, so you can inspect where the loop went.

nodes.title: Rewrite the method
nodes.tip: Browser behaviour, not the RFC: a POST answered with 302 is re-sent as a GET. HEAD is never changed. Only 307 and 308 keep the original method.

nodes.title: Drop the body unless 307 / 308
nodes.tip: Content-Length, Content-Type and Transfer-Encoding are removed with it. For 307/308 a file body is rewound so it can be sent again.

nodes.title: Strip Authorization if host changed
lines: http→https on standard ports keeps it
nodes.tip: Stops a redirect from leaking your token to another site. A change of port or scheme also strips it, except the http:80 → https:443 upgrade. Netrc credentials for the new host are added back if trust_env is on.

nodes.title: Rebuild cookies and proxies
nodes.tip: The old Cookie header is dropped and rebuilt from the jar, including cookies the redirect response just set. Proxy settings are recomputed for the new URL.

nodes.title: Send again, no auto-redirect
nodes.tip: Calls Session.send() with allow_redirects=False. If the answer is another redirect, the loop goes round again.

edges.tip: The response joins history before the count is checked.

edges.label: yes
edges.tip: Limit set by Session.max_redirects.

edges.label: no
edges.tip: Works on a copy of the previous PreparedRequest.
A method rewritten to GET almost always loses its body here too.
Header changes continue on the same copy.
Credentials settled; now session state.
The rewritten request goes back through the adapter path.

edges.label: another redirect
edges.tip: The loop continues while each response is itself a redirect.

blocks.alt: Your code posts with a bearer token to api.example.com, gets a 302 to cdn.example.net, and requests re-sends as GET without the token.

sections.heading: Where each setting can come from

blocks.text: A per-call argument beats a Session attribute, which beats the environment. But not every setting exists at every level, and the gaps explain some common bugs.

blocks.title: Per-call, Session or environment?
blocks.alt: Three overlapping sets: per-call arguments, Session attributes and environment variables, with each setting placed in the region of the levels that can set it.
blocks.caption: Timeout sits alone: there is no session-wide or environment timeout, so every call needs its own.

sets.title: Per-call argument
sets.tip: Keyword arguments to get(), post(), request() and friends.

sets.title: Session attribute
sets.tip: Set once on a Session object and applied to every request it sends.

sets.title: Environment
sets.tip: Read only when Session.trust_env is True, which is the default.

regions.tip: Must be passed on every call.

items.tip: No default: without it a call can wait forever. Probed: still waiting after 4 s on a silent server.
True for every helper except head().
The body is always per call.
The only way to turn on retries: mount an HTTPAdapter(max_retries=...).

regions.empty: Nothing is environment-only: every environment value can be overridden in code.

regions.tip: Merged: per-call keys win, session keys fill in.

items.tip: Dictionaries are merged key by key; set a key to None per call to remove a session value.
Simple values: the per-call one wins if given.

regions.empty: Every environment-backed setting is also a Session attribute.
Every environment-backed setting can also be passed per call.

regions.tip: All three levels; environment fills in only what code left unset.

items.tip: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or CURL_CA_BUNDLE, only when verify is True or unset.
From ~/.netrc when no auth is set in code.

cells: A silent server hangs your program. Always pass `timeout=`.
Each call opens and closes its own Session. Use one Session for many calls to the same host.
One failed connect is final. Mount an HTTPAdapter with max_retries to retry.
More concurrent threads than this on one Session open extra connections that are thrown away after use.
Use 307/308 on the server if the method must survive.
Environment proxies, CA bundle and ~/.netrc apply silently. Set `session.trust_env = False` to ignore them.
